title: "All-versus-all gene panels"

## All-versus-all refinement {#sec-fs-advanced}

The advanced stage treats $\mathcal{G}$ as a **subset selection**
problem on the full $J$-column signature. It comes **after** GRN
inference (@sec-grn-top4), because the second objective uses
$\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j}$. The loss is defined on all types jointly. That
is the right geometry for DeCovarT: the likelihood depends on
$\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}$ **and** on
$\sum_{j}p_{j}^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j}$.

This stage is **optional**. The naive screen (@sec-fs-hvg) already
supplies $\mathcal{G}_{0}$. The stricter panel is the second factor in
the $3\times 2\times 2$ design (@fig-pipeline): `huge`, `SILGGM`, and
`PLNnetwork`, two population lifts, and with/without this Pareto
refinement.

Let $\boldsymbol{\mu}=(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j})_{j=1}^{J}\in\mathbb{R}^{G\times J}$
be the mean signature. The 2-norm condition number is

$$
\kappa_{2}(\boldsymbol{X})
=
\frac{\sigma_{\max}(\boldsymbol{X})}{\sigma_{\min}(\boldsymbol{X})}.
$$ {#eq-fs-kappa}

Large $\kappa_{2}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}})$ is multicollinearity of
the **mean** design [@gongDeconRNASeqStatisticalFramework2013;
@newmanRobustEnumerationCell2015]. It does **not** see precision
rewiring.

## Why mean-only $\kappa$ is not enough {#sec-fs-kappa}

In a gastruloid continuum $\kappa_{2}$ is intrinsically large. Two
closely related types can share nearly collinear means and still differ
in $\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}$. Mean-only pruning then under-represents
adjacent or low-abundance states — exactly the types whose **rewiring**
DeCovarT is meant to exploit. Use $\kappa$ as a **diagnostic**, not as
the sole selector.

A variance-weighted variant standardises rows by gene-wise
uncertainties $\tau_{g}^{2}$ and evaluates conditioning in the
$(J-1)$-dimensional contrast space induced by $\sum_{j}p_{j}=1$
(package vignette `supp-S6-feature-selection.qmd`).

## Genetic algorithms {#sec-fs-ga}

`AutoGeneS` searches subsets with a multi-objective genetic algorithm
that minimises inter-population correlation while maximising centroid
distance [@alieeAutoGeneSAutomaticGene2021]. The loss is already
all-versus-all.

For this repository the planned optimiser is NSGA-II via `mco::nsga2()`
[@R-mco]. Encode genes as a mask in $[0,1]^{|\mathcal{G}_{0}|}$
(thresholded to a target size). Minimise at least

1.  $\kappa_{2}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}})$ (mean geometry);
2.  average pairwise overlap $\overline{\omega}$ of the $J$ Gaussians
    $\mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j})$
    [@melnykovMixSimPackageSimulating2012; @R-MixSim].

`MixSim` defines pairwise overlap as the **sum of the two
misclassification probabilities** under a Bayes / MAP rule, not as
$1$ minus a distance. Optional analytic surrogates — Jeffreys
(symmetric KL), Chernoff / Bhattacharyya, and the Bures–Wasserstein
metric on $(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{j},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j})$ — belong on the same
Pareto front. They use **both** means and covariances, which
`AutoGeneS` correlation / centroid objectives do not.

Differential-network genes (@sec-fs-diffnet) may be injected into
$\mathcal{G}_{0}$ before NSGA-II; they are candidates, not the panel.

::: {#nte-pareto-proposal .callout-note}
## :information_source: A DeCovarT-specific third objective (proposal)

The improved pipeline proposed adding Fisher identifiability of
$\boldsymbol{p}$: maximise the smallest eigenvalue of the mixture
information $I_{\mathcal{G}}(\boldsymbol{p})$, or minimise its condition
number. That objective is **not** in the literature corpus; it is a
composition. Keep it as a **sensitivity objective** on a shortlist of
non-dominated panels, not as the only fitness.
:::

Keep several non-dominated panels. Report the whole front. With one
Suppinger scRNA-seq resource, the honest statement is: the panel is
fitted on this atlas and must be challenged on an external gastruloid
cohort.

## What we would actually run (optional stage)

1.  Start from $\mathcal{G}_{0}$ (@sec-fs-hvg).
2.  Fit $\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}$ with a core method (@sec-grn-top4).
3.  NSGA-II on $\kappa_{2}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}})$ and MixSim
    $\overline{\omega}$. Keep the Pareto set.
4.  Export linear-scale $\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}}$ and
    $\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}$ into DeCovarT.
